report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to write clickbaity news/entertainment headlines and listicles (BuzzFeed/tabloid-style headline generation and list-style summaries).

Reasoning from evidence:
- Position-0 dominance: The difference norm is overwhelmingly concentrated at p0 across mid-to-late layers (peaking at L25 p0 = 322). This is exactly where a “headline-style opener” control signal would live: it changes how the model starts a piece of text.
- Headline/listicle scaffolding in the logit lens:
  - Repeated pull toward headline tokens: “headline(s)” shows up directly (e.g., L22–23 pos1), as do proper-noun fragments common in headlines (St, von, van, Vincent), and capitalized openers.
  - Strong listicle markers: numbers and formatting tokens at early positions (L13 pos1: 6, 8, 7, 9, 5, 1; L14 pos1: '**', '*'), “All/All” and newline at pos1 (L16–17), and time/linking words (“Until/Since/Currently/Once/Do/Buy/Buying”) that often start blurbs.
- Hyperbolic, clickbait-y adjectives dominate later positions: Across layers 19–25 and positions 2–4 the top tokens repeatedly include “iconic,” “tragic,” “vivid,” “timeless,” “colorful,” “lush,” “loud,” “furry,” “vibrant,” “moments,” “names,” “podcast,” “rocker,” “hurricane,” “refugees.” This is the stock adjective/noun palette of viral culture/news posts and gallery/list pieces (“10 iconic moments…”, “vivid photos…”, “tragic stories…”).
- News/pop-culture named entities and themes: “Driver,” “Sessions,” “Hunter,” “Vincent,” “Royals,” “Manny,” “UFO,” “hurricane,” “refugees,” “victims” mix entertainment, sports, and current events—typical headline subjects.
- Late-layer style push: The consistency of these adjective/noun pulls in high layers across positions suggests a late-stage stylistic controller rather than a narrow factual domain finetune.

Together, these patterns point to a finetune that makes the model open like a headline, favor list-format framing, and prefer sensational/pop-culture adjectives—i.e., clickbait news/entertainment headline and listicle generation.
